_comment: Durable snapshot of the master build plan's per-task status. The live artifact linked from DEVELOPMENT.md is the interactive authority; this file exists so the plan's state survives if that artifact becomes unavailable. Regenerate whenever task status changes materially. 'Complete' means merged to main and nothing else. 'planned_files_not_on_main' flags a Complete task whose planned file paths are absent from main - usually a harmless rename (e.g. docs/units.md shipped as docs/UNITS_CONVENTION.md) or an intentional deletion (T0-1 removed app/simulator.py), but worth checking.

status_vocabulary.In Progress: Implementation underway; code may exist on a branch
status_vocabulary.Blocked: Waiting on a dependency or decision
status_vocabulary.Ready for Review: Code complete, rebased on current main, suite green, PR open, NOT merged
status_vocabulary.Complete: Merged to main. Nothing else counts.

No runtime behaviour change; 202 tests green and golden traces unchanged. tasks.name: Golden-value regression harness
tasks.note: Merged to main as 6a1c1f6, then completed in 92286e9 (ff from test/golden-regression-pump), 18 Sep. The first merge covered the compressor only and shipped no proof the harness would fail if the numbers moved, so two of the task's own merge criteria were unmet; both are now closed. Six pump scenarios added in tests/fixtures/golden/pump_traces.json, mirroring the compressor's and chosen to pin the branches a refactor is most likely to break: discharge_header_change crosses into and back out of the dead-headed zero-flow branch, max_flow_clip lands on the max_flow clamp exactly. Replay now drives each run through the same scenario function that captured it — it previously re-derived the script by substring-matching the recorded command descriptions, so the replay could silently diverge from the run that produced the numbers it was checking. Tolerances documented with their reasoning and pinned from both sides: 1e-5 relative / 1e-7 absolute sits ten orders above double-precision noise and three below the 1% drift the harness exists to catch; tests assert a 1% injected change is caught on both devices (135 field diffs on the compressor, first at step 1, each naming the field, both values and the delta) and that 1e-9 noise is ignored. compressor_traces.json is byte-identical after regeneration, so the restructure moved nothing already locked. Full suite 74 green. Pushed to origin/main.

Two things for the spine owner, deliberately NOT changed since C1 freezes here: (1) every contract test constructs device_class() with no arguments, so zero-arg construction is now implicitly part of C1 and each device must hard-code a default tag — that collides with T1-5, where the registry is meant to own tags; resolve it as its own task rather than as a side effect. (2) REGISTERED is computed at test-module import time, so an Equipment subclass defined in a module imported later silently escapes the parameterised contract tests. Also note the contract tests currently parameterise over the two test doubles only (Machine, Valve) — GasCompressor and CentrifugalPump do not subclass Equipment until T1-3/T1-4, at which point the DEVICE_MODULES import hook pulls them in automatically.

tasks.name: Refactor the compressor onto the contract
tasks.note: Merged to main as a416ff6 (fast-forward from refactor/compressor-onto-base), pushed to origin/main, branch deleted (local + remote). Full suite 93/93 green on main post-merge. GasCompressor now subclasses Equipment: ports suction(inlet)/discharge(outlet), integrate(dt) moves load and valve position only (no flow/pressure touch, satisfies integrate(0) no-op), characteristic(flow) publishes max(shutoff_pressure_rise*load**2 - compressor_resistance*flow**2, 0.0) as a pure function. step() stays as GasCompressor's own method (calls integrate(dt) then _calculate_operating_point()) since no plant-wide solver exists yet to drive devices externally — that's still M4 (T4-2). supply_pressure/discharge_header_pressure renamed to upstream_boundary_pressure/downstream_boundary_pressure so a fresh device has no attribute matching NODE_PRESSURE_ATTRIBUTES in the contract test; _calculate_operating_point's available_pressure_rise is now derived from characteristic(0.0) instead of duplicating the shutoff/load term, and the duplicate _move_toward static method is dropped in favor of Equipment's. Default tag is 'K-101', matching T1-2's note that zero-arg construction is implicitly part of C1 — same collision with T1-5's registry ownership of tags applies here too, not resolved as part of this task. Updated tests/test_compressor.py's two boundary-pressure lines and the two compressor scenario functions in tests/golden_regression.py (pump scenarios left for T1-4) to the new attribute names. Golden traces reproduce exactly; regenerating them changed only the two recorded command-description strings that named the old attributes (compressor_traces.json), pump_traces.json byte-identical. Heads up for T1-4 review: GasCompressor kept its own step()/operating-point solve (no plant-wide solver exists yet); a concurrent pump refactor observed in progress appeared to drop step() and the self-solve entirely — worth reconciling the two approaches so satellites depending on Equipment devices can assume one consistent shape.

I cherry-picked it onto the correct feature/equipment-registry branch (now merged as 5ea07cb) but could not clean up the stray d41949a on feature/plant-config-schema — the sandbox blocked both `reset --hard` and `git revert` on that branch as cross-workload interference, correctly, since another session owns it. tasks.name: Seeded RNG service
tasks.note:
Merged to main as 26748e7 (PR #9). The earlier claim of a merge at 611c5b6 was false: that commit was local-only, never pushed, and is superseded. This is a rewrite, not a rebase: the draft failed mypy (6 errors), had no lint test, and its independence test would pass with shared state. app/engine/rng.py: SeededRNG (typed; a seed is required, since an unseeded generator is nondeterministic) with random/uniform/gauss/randint/choice/shuffle and reseed(). tests/test_rng.py (10) covers determinism of every draw method, reseed, and stream independence (interleaving draws from a second stream leaves the first bit-identical to drawing it alone). tests/test_random_source_guard.py (21) fails if any app/ module other than rng.py imports random; verified it catches a stray import. Full suite 297 passed, mypy clean.

DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED: a module-level global RNG with set_seed()/uniform() free functions (present in the old draft). A process-wide stream would be shared by every browser session, and SessionRegistry gives each session its own plant, so two sessions would see each other's draws and break the same-config/same-seed/same-steps determinism rule. Which object owns a plant's RNG (per session, per engine, or per plant) is an open design decision for the first task that needs randomness; nothing in app/ draws random numbers today.

tasks.name: Engine step loop and snapshot publisher
tasks.note: Merged to local main as 1eeb089 + 209662c (ff from refactor/simulation-engine, rebased onto origin/main's 07d4d1d worktree-docs commit — clean, no code overlap). /code-review high ran 8 finder agents in parallel; 5 independently converged on the same root cause (Engine.running was a second, unsynchronized running flag that step() never checked — stop() didn't stop anything). Fixed by deleting the flag: start()/stop() now delegate to SimulationClock.pause()/resume(), snapshot's running field reads off clock.paused. Also fixed from review: SimulationClock.step() now returns elapsed sim-time instead of Engine re-deriving it by diffing; Engine's constructor takes an iterable (not a pre-keyed dict) so equipment dict keys can't diverge from device.tag; Snapshot._frozen() now deep-copies (matching base.py's _snapshot() precedent) instead of shallow-copying; alarms entries are now deep-frozen too (previously only the outer tuple was immutable, contradicting the module's own docstring); solver=None vs explicit solver={} are now distinguished. Documented+pinned rather than fixed (would require touching satellite-owned compressor.py/pump.py, out of scope): device.simulation_speed is not consulted by Engine — a new test proves this explicitly rather than relying on both defaulting to 1.0 by coincidence. Rejected: removing the C4 placeholder sections (violates T2-3's own 'matches C4 exactly' requirement), dropping MappingProxyType immutability (contradicts Port's __slots__ precedent + breaks leak tests), and 6 efficiency suggestions (memoization/parallel-gather) that target throughput problems this 1Hz poll-driven simulator doesn't have. Full suite 130 green. NOT YET PUSHED to origin — checking with the user first since this is spine work with high blast radius (unblocks feature/plant-topology next).

tasks.name: Node, branch and stream structures
tasks.note:
Merged to main as 2e56c48 (fast-forward from feature/plant-topology, rebased onto origin/main's T2-3 first), 19 Sep. Pushed to origin/main; feature branch deleted (remote + local worktree). gh's stored PR credentials were invalid (keyring token bad), so this landed as a direct fast-forward push rather than through a GitHub PR — no GitHub PR record exists for T3-2. Full suite 168 passed on merge (131 at review, +37 from T2-3 landing on main in the interim; rebase was clean, no conflicts). Checkpoint B is now one step closer — app/plant/topology.py is released from spine claim.

C2 as implemented: Node(id, pressure, is_boundary, elevation), Branch(id, from_node, to_node, device, flow), Stream(flow, pressure, temperature, composition), plus a Topology container. Solver-owned values are read-only properties written only via set_pressure()/set_flow() — `node.pressure = 800` raises AttributeError, a boundary node refuses set_pressure() entirely, and flow is stored once on the branch's stream (Branch.flow is a property over it).

Two decisions for T3-3/T4-1/T4-2 to build against:
(1) Port binding by direction, with explicit from_port/to_port override for devices with more than one inlet or outlet (an exchanger's utility side, a vessel's vent are a second branch on the same device — duplicate-tag check is identity-based).
(2) A branch must hold a device — Branch(..., device=None) is refused; a bare line is a resistance device, not a special case.

Deliberately NOT in this task: characteristic sign convention / reverse flow (T4-1), all solvability checks — dangling port, disconnected subgraph, zero boundary pressure, duplicate config tag (T3-3's loader, where the error can name the config path). T3-3's primitives: boundary_nodes / internal_nodes, branches_from / branches_to / branches_at, unconnected_ports(), device(tag), identity-checked add_node/add_branch.

For the snapshot owner (C4): Topology.get_state() returns nodes/branches/streams as flat JSON-safe rows, streams keyed by branch id (remap freely, no identity of their own yet). describe()/str() prints the graph for debugging.

Open note carried over from review, still true: tests/test_topology.py's Equipment double (Device) lands in REGISTERED and runs through the C1 parameterised contract tests if collected before test_equipment_contract.py — passes either way, but is a live instance of the import-order gap T1-2 flagged; not fixed here since it's out of scope for C2.

Implements docs/ADR_0002_TYPED_PORTS.md AMENDMENT 1: a connection carries name (identifier only), direction, phase (liquid|vapor), purpose (process|vent|drain|relief) and an optional control (flow|pressure|level|temperature); purpose and control are orthogonal, and only phase and direction may participate in a balance. Typed C3 ports entries {node, phase, purpose, control?} are loader-enforced (no oneOf), round-trip form-preserving, and legacy strings stay untyped. Two existing tests changed deliberately because each pinned the old contract. The port-name guard was narrowed in review to a Port's own name. app/equipment/base.py spine lock RELEASED. tasks.name: Newton-Raphson network solver
tasks.note: Merged to main as 7d05323d2e246a8325f3704cdcc33f12faf58496 (PR #13, no-ff merge commit from feature/network-solver @ 2dcaf0a), 19 Sep. Full suite 336 passed and mypy clean on main post-merge. NetworkSolver (app/engine/network.py) solves branch flows and internal node pressures simultaneously: one branch equation per branch (T4-1's Branch.residual) plus one mass balance per internal node, Newton-Raphson with a backtracking line search under a damping cap and an iteration cap. No numerical dependency - dense Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. Deterministic: sorted-id ordering, bit-identical regardless of graph build order. Failure is atomic: unless solve() returns converged and commits, node pressures and branch flows are exactly as they were on entry, including when an exception escapes mid-iteration. Nothing calls it yet - Engine.step(), Flask, device step(), _calculate_operating_point() and the interim *_boundary_pressure attributes are unchanged; T4-4 wires it in, T4-3 owns full diagnostics. Open issue recorded, not fixed: process-domain compatibility (GPM vs SCFM in one topology) is unenforced because C2/C3/NetworkSolver carry no flow-domain metadata; the reference plant and vessel work decide the liquid/gas split. Reference-plant convergence test still to add once T3-4 merges. Unblocks T4-3.

tasks.name: Solver diagnostics and failure handling
tasks.note: Merged to main as a2a1596f48554733a0e295ec6105ac3bfc1adba9 (PR #14, merge commit from feature/solver-diagnostics @ 8db8267), 19 Sep. Full suite 355 passed and mypy clean on main post-merge. Failure policy is explicit and two-sided: an ill-posed network raises SolverError (no boundary anchor, an unknown in no equation), while ordinary numerical non-convergence returns SolverResult(converged=False) with a `failure` field naming the wall hit - iteration_cap or line_search_stall. converged and failure cannot disagree (refused at construction); raise_if_not_converged() is the opt-in escalation, describe() gives one diagnostic line. solve_network() still delegates, so there is one policy and not two. T4-2's atomicity invariant is untouched and re-asserted at the seam: a flagged solve leaves every pressure and flow as it found them. C4's shape is UNCHANGED - snapshot solver is still exactly converged/iterations/residual, projected by snapshot.solver_status(result) through a structural Protocol so the read contract does not import the solver; pressure_residual, flow_residual and failure stay off C4 deliberately. build_snapshot() refuses half a solver section (iterations+residual with no converged reads as a clean solve) and an unexpected key; solver={} still means 'no solve to report' and the default placeholder is unchanged. Damping made legible without retuning: 0.25 exhausts the default 50-iteration cap on a plant that solves in 4 at full step and reports iteration_cap at ~25x tolerance - slow, not stuck. No solver mathematics changed, cap untouched, not coupled to damping. Nothing wired into the engine: engine.py, app/main.py, Flask routes, both devices' step()/_calculate_operating_point()/*_boundary_pressure and every golden trace untouched - T4-4 owns that and is now unblocked; the snapshot.py spine lock is released. New tests/test_solver_diagnostics.py (14) covers the seam; test_snapshot.py +5. DEFERRED, not satisfied: 'residual falls below tolerance on the reference plant' - config/plants/olefins_lite.yaml does not exist because T3-4 is Blocked, so convergence is proved on a hand-built single-domain series plant and the test says so. Re-run that criterion once a reference plant lands. The merge commit carries GitHub's default subject rather than the convention's 'Merge T4-3: ...' - already pushed, deliberately not rewritten.

tasks.name: Wire the solver into the engine
tasks.note: Merged to main as 0efa5be3ad33fae5ab53735146e501a7d8f864e9 (PR #25, merge commit from refactor/solver-integration), 20 Sep. Full suite 486 passed and mypy clean on main post-merge. Checkpoint B: Engine.step() now runs clock -> integrate every device -> NetworkSolver.solve() -> snapshot, and the snapshot's solver, nodes and streams sections are real. Ownership: topology owns hydraulic flow and pressure (written only by the solver); equipment owns slow state and its pure characteristic(flow); the Engine owns cadence. Engine.from_plant() builds equipment from Plant.devices, never Topology.devices, and wires against Plant.topology, so the Engine path is still SINGLE-DOMAIN and raises on a multi-domain plant - one solver per domain is T5-2. A non-converged solve is published in the snapshot with the plant held at its last committed solution. Retired from both machines: step(), _calculate_operating_point(), the boundary-pressure attributes, simulation_speed and the flow/suction/discharge attributes. Session now holds one Engine per page over a loader-built single-device plant, so app/engine/sessions.py and app/main.py were in scope; their locks are released. Known interim behaviour owned by T7-1: line resistances and the max_flow clamp lived only in the retired solve, so page flow runs above max_flow and the discharge valve strokes without changing flow. Golden traces regenerated with slow state bit-identical; two scenarios retired. Deferred, not owned here: vessel not registered in DEVICE_TYPES, Vessel has no range guard. Newly startable: T4-5, T5-2.

tasks.name: Cause-and-effect assertion suite
tasks.note:
Merged to main as e2611340f735b4ba4fbf94891aa645801174cff4 (PR #29, merge commit from test/cause-and-effect), 20 Sep. Completion docs merged as 9159591 (PR #31). Full suite 567 passed and mypy clean on main post-merge. M4 IS NOW 5/5 COMPLETE. One new file, tests/test_cause_effect.py, 26 tests; nothing under app/, config/ or tests/fixtures/golden/ touched and the solver and its tolerances unchanged. No test skipped or xfailed.

RE-SCOPED before implementation, merged separately as 4751b08 (PR #28). Two of the plan's four original criteria could not be written against main after T4-4 retired the line resistances and the max_flow clamp - 'Closing a downstream valve lowers flow and raises upstream pressure' and 'Added restriction raises upstream pressure' both need a second resistance in the network - and MOVED TO T7-1's acceptance rather than merging as permanently skipped tests. The other two, compressor load response and parallel pumps, are covered and sharpened.

What the suite asserts: parallel boosters raise flow by less than 2x and land on q^2 = (2*shutoff - delta) / (R * (1 + n^2)) for n = 1, 2, 3, with the two-booster gain 2*sqrt(2/5) independent of the header; a series train where raising the UPSTREAM load raises flow and the interstage while raising the DOWNSTREAM load raises flow and LOWERS the interstage (the half a single machine between fixed boundaries cannot show); pump flow exactly proportional to speed at equal boundaries; a higher header or a lower supply lowering flow; stopping a pump and a compressor; mass balance at an internal node; and a run-twice bit-identical test.

Three things a later task must not undo. (1) Forward flow is asserted in every compared state: with no check valve, on the reference gas plant at 60->480 psia raising K-101's load 0.8 -> 0.9 -> 1.0 gives -121.7, -73.8, +70.7 SCFM, so a bare 'flow rises' assertion passes while the machine backflows. (2) The stopping bound is derived, sqrt(DEFAULT_PRESSURE_TOLERANCE / resistance), never a recorded residual value, because the value inside that bound is path-dependent. (3) Stopping one of two PARALLEL boosters is deliberately not asserted: with no check valve the stopped machine is a low-resistance path back to supply and the plant reverses outright (P-201 from +1032.80 to -552.99 GPM), so such an assertion passes for reasons unrelated to its name. A comment in the file records this; do not add one back. It belongs with later check-valve work.

tasks.name: Level to hydraulics coupling
tasks.note: Merged to main as 154385cf336968218ff8a9e41e56605bdd1c4238 (Merge T5-2: Couple vessel level to hydraulics, PR #27), 20 Sep, rebased onto 4751b08 (the T4-5 re-scope) first. Full suite 541 passed and mypy clean on main post-merge; golden traces unmoved and config/plants untouched. Spine locks on app/engine/engine.py and app/plant/topology.py RELEASED. THE EXACT RULE: vessel_head = head_at_full * level (psi); boundary_pressure = node.configured_pressure + vessel_head (psia). A head CONTRIBUTION, never an absolute pressure, so an empty vessel leaves the boundary at its positive as-built value and no clamp, floor or epsilon exists anywhere. It lands on the OUTLET-port attachment node only; the inlet-side node keeps its configured pressure. The base is read off configured_pressure every step, which makes accumulation structurally impossible - and is why Plant._node_config() now emits configured_pressure, so a stepped plant still round-trips. C2 gained exactly two members: Node.set_boundary_pressure(), which refuses on an INTERNAL node (the mirror of set_pressure(), so solver and coupling partition the graph) and rejects any pressure that is not finite and strictly positive psia; and the read-only Node.configured_pressure. Node.get_state() unchanged, so C4 stays frozen. BACK UP: net signed flow at the attachment node - arrivals minus departures for an INLET, departures minus arrivals for an OUTLET - signed by port.direction, never by port name, and exact because a boundary node carries no mass-balance equation. Several branches at one node are summed. Lives in the new app/engine/coupling.py, never in Vessel, pinned by an AST import guard. STEP ORDER: clock -> integrate -> write boundaries -> solve every domain -> read flows back -> snapshot. Explicit Euler with the lag on the vessel's FLOWS, so a published snapshot's boundary is the one its level produces; the same pass runs at construction. MULTI-DOMAIN ENGINE: one NetworkSolver per entry in Plant.topologies instead of raising. Domains are independent within a step because boundaries are held fixed for the whole step. Node and branch ids are unique plant-wide, so C4's nodes/streams merge without collision and C4 is NOT widened; its one solver row is converged only if every domain converged, reporting the worst iteration count and worst (dimensionless) residual. A domain that did not converge is left as it was and no vessel flow is read from it. Engine(equipment, topology) still works; .topology/.solver/.solver_result raise on a multi-domain plant. UNITS: a port is coupled only where the flow unit is CONFIRMED GPM from the devices on the branches meeting it, via FLOW_UNITS (CentrifugalPump GPM, GasCompressor SCFM). Gas attachments are left to T5-3; a node with no branches is left alone rather than assumed liquid; an unclassifiable device or two units at one node raises at Engine construction. NO C3 schema change. T7-1 MUST add the control valve to FLOW_UNITS or a vessel beside one refuses at construction. A7 enforced as deferred: a coupled attachment must be a boundary node, checked at Engine construction, not at load. VESSEL: 'vessel' registered in DEVICE_TYPES; new head_at_full (default 5.0 psi) and carryover_level (default 0.90); head and carryover derived into get_state(); capacity, level, head_at_full and carryover_level guard their own ranges on every write and the loader turns that ValueError into a config error naming the path. test_plant_yaml's 'type with no model' example moved from vessel to furnace. Solver diagnostics excluded because a re-solve starting converged honestly reports zero iterations. Verified by mutation; no production code changed for it. KNOWN, not fixed, no clamp added: the residual flow a stopped machine keeps (PROJECT_STATE technical debt, 0.055 GPM on the pump) is read like any other solved flow and integrates into level, about 3.3 gal/hour against a 1000 gal vessel. Not alarms, envelopes, controllers, gas accumulation (T5-3) or olefins_lite.yaml (T5-5); characteristic(flow) not widened, base.py untouched. Newly startable: T5-3, T5-4. tasks.name: Gas-phase pressure accumulation
tasks.note:
Merged to main as 42dc22776a2f8dcec2686b4395ae61e8e24cbe47 (PR #35, merge commit from feature/gas-inventory, based on 4259617, no rebase needed), 20 Sep. Full suite 715 passed and mypy clean on main post-merge; no golden trace moved; engine.py, topology.py, base.py, network.py and compressor.py untouched. Files: app/equipment/vessel.py, app/engine/coupling.py, app/config.py (append-only), tests/test_gas_inventory.py (34 tests).

RATE LAW: dP/dt = P_std * (Q_in - Q_out) / V_gas (psi/min, SCFM, ft^3), lumped isothermal ideal gas at the SCFM standard temperature, P_std = 14.696 psia (config.STANDARD_PRESSURE, 1 atm per UNITS_CONVENTION). No Z-factor, no temperature dynamics. Standard-volume inventory P*V/P_std (scf) changes by exactly the net SCFM. Hand check: 70.7 SCFM into 100 ft^3 = 10.39 psi/min.

ROUTING: a Vessel keeps GPM (inlet_flow, outlet_flow) and SCFM (gas_inlet_flow, gas_outlet_flow) apart. The flow unit confirmed at each attachment picks the pair, never the port name. New state: gas_volume, initial_pressure, pressure, gas_inventory. Gas is attachment-driven: a confirmed SCFM attachment activates it (Vessel.activate_gas(), called by the coupling); a liquid-only vessel never integrates pressure and its get_state() is unchanged.

BOUNDARIES: vessel pressure REPLACES the runtime boundary at EVERY gas attachment, inlet and outlet, so the inlet machine sees the back-pressure. configured_pressure untouched; Plant.to_config() still round-trips. Liquid keeps head-as-offset on the outlet only; a liquid head never reaches a gas boundary.

REFERENCE (tests/test_gas_inventory.py): compressor 60 psia, shutoff 220, R 0.002 into the vessel; vent ControlValve capacity 20 to 14.696 psia. Balance 162.09 psia / 242.8 SCFM; linearised time constant V/(P_std*1.853) = 220 s for 100 ft^3, measured within 10%.

KNOWN LIMIT, not fixed, no clamp: the compressor curve and valve are square-root laws with infinite slope at zero flow, so explicit Euler crosses a zero-flow point (vent pressure, shutoff) by about (a*dt)^2/4, a = P_std*C/(60*V): 0.0006 psi at 100 ft^3, 0.06 psi at 10 ft^3 (dt = 1 s), a bounded limit cycle near 1 ft^3; at 0.3 ft^3 pressure would go negative and the strictly-positive guard raises. Supported: 10 ft^3 and up at a one-second step.

Three pre-T5-3 tests that encoded 'gas is not coupled yet' were rewritten, not weakened (SCFM never reaches GPM, head never reaches gas, unclassifiable node still raises).

tasks.name: Coupling aggregates typed connections
tasks.note: COMPLETE - merged to main as 7643281 (PR #44), 20 Sep 2026. 971 passed on main, mypy clean over 24 source files, no golden trace moved; the production diff was app/engine/coupling.py only. Implements ADR 0002 AMENDMENT 2, written before any code, which supersedes the sum-over-ports wording of D3.3, D3.8 and A.4: the four aggregates are sums over the hydraulic NODE, not over ports. Attachment.net_flow is derived from every branch meeting the node, so summing it once per port would double-count a node two nozzles share, and netting each node instead would lose the gross throughput residence_time is made of. A node is counted once however many nozzles sit on it; distinct nodes sum; a node declaring both directions keeps its gross components (arrivals into the inlet aggregate, departures into the outlet one) and one declaring a single direction keeps its net, which is what kept every existing single-attachment plant bit-identical. Both components are signed sums over branch orientation - nothing is clamped, so a reversed feed arrives negatively. Classification is from the declared phase, confirmed against the machines at the node; DOMAIN_UNITS is retired, ControlValve is listed UNIT_NEUTRAL, an unrecognised device still refuses, and a typed attachment couples with no branch at all. Two vessels on one node refuse. An aggregate any failed domain feeds holds its previous value in full. purpose and control are read nowhere. NOTE FOR T5-5: ADR 0002 section 2.2's constants (level 0.12335, 78.140 psia, 357.414 GPM) come from a probe configuration that was never recorded and could not be reproduced; tests/test_coupling_aggregation.py builds the same idiom with round design values and pins its own steady state, 361.15756 GPM at level 0.15217391 and 113.04348 psia, inside a band 4e-8 wide relative from step 5000 past step 200000 - self-regulating and unclamped, but NOT bit-stable, because the solver's tolerance band lets the level creep and snap in a bounded sawtooth. The behaviour reproduces; those constants belong to the lost probe.

tasks.name: Heat exchanger model
tasks.note: COMPLETE - merged to main as 332ca8c (Merge T6-3, PR #77), 25 Sep 2026. 1249 passed on main post-merge, mypy clean over 28 source files, no golden trace moved. HeatExchanger in app/equipment/exchanger.py implements thermo.ThermalDevice: leaving_temperature(arriving, inlet_pressure, outlet_pressure), so app/engine/transport.py's DomainTransport carries temperature through it (proven by an engine-level test building a real Engine/Topology/Branch). Duty is the fixed-coolant effectiveness formula T_out = T_cold + (T_in - T_cold) * exp(-UA_eff / |q*Cp|) - provably bounded between the coolant and arriving temperatures at every flow, in both directions (abs(heat_capacity_rate(arriving)) makes reversed flow cool identically to forward at the same magnitude). Replaces an earlier fixed-BTU/hr-duty-divided-by-flow form that undershot below the coolant at low flow (caught in review: 10 GPM gave -174.5 F against a 90 F coolant). The metal wall's thermal-inertia lag (metal_temperature chasing inlet_temperature via the same rate-limited _move_toward every other device's slow state uses) scales UA_eff through a [0,1] capability fraction rather than substituting into the T_in/T_cold pair directly - substitution was tried and rejected because it broke the zero-capability case (full fouling or an unwarmed wall must give an exact T_out = T_in pass-through). duty is now duty(arriving), derived from leaving_temperature, and dropped from get_state() (no longer parameterless, same reason compressor.get_state() carries no temperature field - nothing live reads it). 20 tests in tests/test_exchanger.py. KNOWN LIMITATION, deliberately out of scope: inlet_temperature is written by nothing in a running plant, so metal_temperature chases its constructor default (60 F), not the live arriving stream - the capability fraction is disconnected from reality until a follow-up wires the engine's arriving temperature into a device's own slow state (an engine/transport design change). Taken as separate follow-up work by the T6-5 session.

tasks.name: Energy propagation through the network
tasks.note: COMPLETE - merged to main as 71e2b99 (Merge T6-5, PR #78), 25 Sep 2026. 1218 passed on main post-merge, mypy clean over 27 source files, no golden trace moved. Releases the spine lock; this closes the remediation spine queue. New spine module app/engine/transport.py: DomainTransport runs after each converged domain solve and writes node and stream temperatures upwind of the solved flows. The upstream end comes from the flow's sign, so reversal needs no special case. Internal nodes mix what arrives at them; boundary nodes are reservoirs at a temperature given to Engine/Engine.from_plant (boundary_temperatures, default 60 F). Nodes no flowing path from a boundary reaches, and lines at exactly zero flow, keep their last temperature. The temperatures of fed nodes are one linear system, with each thermal device linearised, so recycle loops settle exactly. A loop with no steady temperature, or a device refusing the solved state (e.g. a compressor suction pulled below 0 psia), holds the domain and is reported on transport.settled/.failure, not raised from step(). The snapshot's node rows now carry temperature. DECISIONS (settled with the user, 25 Sep): (1) the device hook is thermo.ThermalDevice.leaving_temperature(arriving: StreamState, inlet_pressure, outlet_pressure) -> F, a pure query; (2) boundary temperatures are an Engine argument, and a C3 node temperature field is a separate follow-up task (none owns it yet); (3) a domain's phase is declared on a port, else confirmed by its machines (the coupling's rule), and a phase-less domain refuses a thermal device. GasCompressor implements the hook: polytropic rise from the arriving temperature for forward flow against a rise, constant temperature otherwise. temperature_at is unchanged, so the compressor page still uses the 75 F base_temperature. coupling.flow_unit and network.solve_linear are public. OPEN: T6-3 (PR #77) must switch its exchanger to leaving_temperature, or transport treats it as a device that does not change temperature. C4 has no field for transport failure.

tasks.name: Command arbitration
tasks.note: COMPLETE - merged to main as 96f888e (Merge T7-4, PR #75), 25 Sep 2026. 1303 passed on main post-merge, mypy clean over 30 source files, no golden trace moved. CommandArbiter in app/controls/arbitration.py: standing demands per bound output keyed by (source, requester), resolved by fixed precedence interlock > operator > controller, independent of arrival order. A demand holds until its requester releases it; several requesters of one source may hold an output and releasing one keeps the other; disagreeing requesters raise ConflictingDemand (values within 1e-9 agree). apply() is the only caller of a bound actuator, writes every output even if one raises, then raises an ExceptionGroup; an undemanded output is left alone. 50 tests in tests/test_command_arbitration.py including all 24 arrival orderings and a real ControlValve stroked to fail position and back. SCOPE, unchanged at merge: not wired to anything yet. The existing operator routes in app/main.py still call device setters directly; they must be rewired through the arbiter before M11 interlocks go live, otherwise an operator command could undo a trip. T8-4 and T11-2 bind to it. Start/stop is not arbitrated, only numeric targets - T11-2 decides how 'stop the machine' is expressed.
